cards.text: Jeremiah, a prophet, is carrying the word of the LORD to His people, Israel, and the LORD is NOT here for small talk. Long ago, He says, they broke their yoke and tore off their chains.

cards.question: Israel breaks the yoke and tears off the chains. What are they saying as they do it?

cards.text: Then comes a hard picture: on every high hill and under every green tree, Israel lay down as a prostitute. And the LORD reminds them He had planted them like a choice vine from the very best seed.

cards.question: The LORD planted Israel like a choice vine. What does He say they turned themselves into?
Israel can wash with lye and plenty of soap, but the ___ of their guilt is still before the LORD.

cards.text: Lye AND an abundance of soap? Friend, I don't scrub my mixing bowls that hard, and it STILL won't come out. Then the LORD repeats what Israel says about the Baals.

cards.question: Israel admits they have run after the Baals.

cards.text: Look at your behavior in the valley, the LORD says. Israel is a swift young she-camel galloping here and there, a wild donkey sniffing the wind in the heat of her desire.

cards.question: In the LORD's picture, anyone looking for that wild donkey has to wear themselves out to find her.

cards.text: The LORD says they should have kept their feet from going bare and their throats from being thirsty. All that galloping here and there? That's me when every oven timer in the bakery goes off at ONCE.

cards.question: Israel could stop chasing. So why do they say it's hopeless?

cards.text: As a thief is ashamed when he's caught, so Israel is disgraced, kings, officials, priests and prophets included. I know that caught face, friend. I make it every time a baker walks in on me with a mustache full of cookie dough.

cards.question: Israel's leaders say to a ___, 'You are my father,' and to a ___, 'You gave me birth.'

cards.text: They've turned their backs to the LORD and not their faces. Yet in the time of trouble, they say, 'Rise up and save us!'

cards.question: Trouble hits, and Israel cries, 'Rise up and save us!' What does the LORD say back?

answers.text: Let the gods they made save them
He is already on His way to them
They should wait for Him at the temple

cards.text: Judah, the LORD says, your gods are as numerous as your cities. A god in EVERY town, friend, and not one of them answering the phone.

cards.question: When Israel brings a case against Him, the LORD says only a few of them have rebelled.
The LORD struck their sons, but they accepted no discipline. And their own ___ devoured their prophets like a voracious lion.

cards.text: Now this generation is told to consider the word of the LORD. And the LORD asks: Has He been a wilderness to Israel, or a land of dense darkness?

cards.question: God's people say they are free to roam and will come to Him no more.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks: Does a maiden forget her jewelry, or a bride her wedding sash? Friend, I've walked out of this bakery without my apron, but NOBODY walks into her own wedding without that sash.

cards.question: A bride never forgets her wedding sash. How long have God's people forgotten Him?

cards.text: The LORD says they pursue love so skillfully, even the most immoral of women could learn from their ways.

cards.question: And their skirts are stained with the blood of the innocent ___.
In spite of all these things, Israel says they are innocent.

cards.text: They even say, 'Surely His anger will turn from me.' That's me with flour all over my mustache going, 'Flour? What flour?'

cards.question: Why does the LORD say He will judge them?

answers.text: Because they say they have not sinned
Because they ran away from Jerusalem

cards.text: The LORD says, 'How impulsive you are, constantly changing your ways!' That's me at the topping station: sprinkles, no, chips, no, WAIT, sprinkles.

cards.question: Israel will be disappointed by Egypt, just as they were by ___.

cards.text: The LORD has rejected those they trust. They will not prosper by their help.

cards.question: So how will Israel leave that place?

answers.text: With their hands on their heads
With their arms full of gold
With a new army behind them

cards.text: Then the LORD asks: If a man divorces his wife and she marries another, can he ever return to her? Wouldn't such a land be completely defiled?

cards.question: Israel has played the harlot with many lovers. What does the LORD ask them?

answers.text: Whether they would return to Him
Whether Egypt will take them in

cards.text: Lift up your eyes to the barren heights, the LORD says. They sat beside the highways waiting for their lovers, like a nomad in the desert, and they defiled the land.

cards.question: Because of that, the showers have been withheld, and no spring ___ have fallen.

cards.text: Yet they have the brazen look of a prostitute and refuse to be ashamed. And they've just called to the LORD, 'My Father, You are my friend from youth.'

cards.question: After calling the LORD 'My Father,' Israel stops doing evil.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 10 mentions chips, a food that isn't a cookie and isn't in the passage.

rule.text: In jokes and comparisons, cookies are the only food he mentions.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't land cleanly. 'I don't scrub my mixing bowls that hard, and it STILL won't come out' blends Papa Dorin's mixing bowls with Israel's stain through an unclear 'it'. The comparison also doesn't share the core action: he says he scrubs less hard, not that his hard scrubbing fails. A stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The question says 'Israel's leaders say to a ___'. In Jeremiah 2:26-27 the speakers are 'They, their kings, their officials, their priests, and their prophets', so the people are included, not only the leaders.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Judah is addressed here for the first time (Jeremiah 2:28), but nothing says who Judah is. Card 1 only introduced Israel, so the switch to 'Judah' is unexplained.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The answers aren't the same kind of thing. The right answer 'sword' is an object, while 'kings' and 'neighbors' are people.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: No story card sets up who killed the prophets. The blank tests the exact wording 'your own sword' rather than meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question types in stop 2 fall into a repeating pattern. Cards 2, 4 and 6 are true or false, multiple choice, then fill in the blank, and cards 7, 9 and 11 repeat the same order.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card mentions blood or the poor. 'innocent poor' versus 'innocent strangers' or 'innocent priests' can only be guessed from wording the baker hasn't seen.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This is a second 'caught with something on my mustache' gag. Stop 1 card 12 already used cookie dough on his mustache, and here it's flour on his mustache. The mustache is becoming a repeated joke source.

rule.text: The mustache is a fact about him, not his main source of jokes.

findings.problem: 'So how will Israel leave that place?' The phrase 'that place' points back to Egypt from a card that is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'Because of that' points back to the defiling of the land, which was told on the previous story card and is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Israel's questions in Jeremiah 3:5 are never told: 'Will He be angry forever? Will He be indignant to the end?' These questions are the point of the contrast with 'you keep doing all the evil you can', so the baker misses the irony that ends the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
